# Example artifacts

**These were generated by the system, not written by hand.**

```bash
node scripts/demo-session.mjs --emit examples/artifacts
```

`scripts/demo-session.mjs` drives the engines through a simulated session — a PR adding
saved-card support to guest checkout. **The software it describes does not exist and no real
testing occurred.** The artefacts are here so you can see the exact shape the system
produces, rather than an approximation of it.

Generating them rather than writing them is deliberate. A system built around "never present
prose as proof of execution" should not ship hand-written examples that look like real
results.

| File | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| [example-report.md](example-report.md) | The rendered report, all 20 sections |
| [example-report.json](example-report.json) | The machine-readable record the Markdown is rendered from |
| [example-execution.json](example-execution.json) | A failed execution with its failure classification |
| [example-decision.json](example-decision.json) | The browser-method decision, with every rejected option and why |
| [example-finding.json](example-finding.json) | A critical finding with reproduction and fingerprint |
| [example-uncertainty.json](example-uncertainty.json) | A blocker, with the work that continued anyway |
| [example-github-issue.md](example-github-issue.md) | The issue body the defect engine renders |
| [example-testing-strategy.md](example-testing-strategy.md) | A project testing strategy (hand-written — it is a human document) |

## What the demo deliberately exercises

The awkward cases, because those are where an agent's honesty actually gets tested:

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Claim `PASSED` with no evidence | Downgraded to `INCONCLUSIVE`, reason recorded |
| Claim `PASSED` with a test report | Stands as `PASSED` |
| A 403 in the output | Classified `authentication-failure` at confidence **0.5** — capped, because it is genuinely ambiguous between a product defect and missing test credentials |
| The same defect recorded twice, worded differently | Second one flagged `duplicate_of` the first, via fingerprint |
| A missing payment credential | Blocker raised; **3 of 4 scenarios still runnable** and run |
| Localisation | `NOT_APPLICABLE` with a reason, as a first-class execution record |
| An execution interrupted mid-run | Recovery marks it `INTERRUPTED`, never infers success |
| A GitHub issue created | Recorded `CONFIRMED` with the issue URL |
| A Jira comment that failed | Recorded **`NOT CONFIRMED`** with the error |
| Assignment attempted with no named account | **Refused** — missing information, not a policy ban |
| Merging a pull request attempted, even with `userAuthorised: true` | **Refused by default** — a different reason: this action cannot be self-authorised at all |

Read section 20 of the report — the integrity self-audit. It states the report's own
false-confidence rate (0) and lists the checks that produced that number.

Read section 1's "What was NOT tested" — 24 items, each with a reason. That section is near
the top, not in an appendix, because a reader who stops after the summary must still know
the boundary of what was covered.

## Regenerating

```bash
node scripts/demo-session.mjs --emit examples/artifacts
```

IDs restart from 1 each run because the demo uses a fresh temporary state directory. To keep
the state and inspect it:

```bash
node scripts/demo-session.mjs --state ./demo-state --emit examples/artifacts
ls demo-state/
```
